answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every identity to lock a refundable stake in escrow before it can trade. Each agent signs its work with a cipher key tied to that stake, so a fake identity is an isolated island: it earns no shared reputation and cannot borrow trust from real agents. Attackers must fund a river of stakes, one per fake, and any fraud forfeits the stake, so creating thousands of identities costs thousands of forfeits instead of nothing.
